titulo: Bing matters twice; the AI bots show up in the server log
titulo_curto: Bing and bots in the log
lead: Bing feeds Copilot and has the only official citations dashboard; and one study found a good share of ChatGPT's citations among the top Bing results. Telling Bing costs little. On the other side, the server log tells you who really reads the site: which AI bots, for what purpose, and which ones are fake.
objetivo: check the site in Bing with IndexNow and read in the log which AI bots really visit, separated by purpose.

aprende.t: The two reasons to care about Bing (and what is a study, not a fact)
Notify IndexNow only with URLs that return 200
Read the log by purpose: search, user action, training
Spot fake bots and CDN blocks in the log

hero_alt: Infrastructure tech looks at a laptop resting on a cart, in a server room.

secoes.titulo: Who finds you, who reads you, who cites you

nos.detalhe: IndexNow tells the participating search engines (Bing among them) that a URL is new or has changed. Google does not participate. Only notify URLs that return 200.

1) Bing feeds Copilot and shows the citations in AI Performance (lesson 2). 2) A study by Seer (about 100 questions, 500+ citations) found 87% of ChatGPT's citations in Bing's top 20, versus 56% in Google. It is a small study, not a statement from OpenAI.
Each line shows the IP, path, response and User-Agent. It is the only source that shows which AI bots reached your site. It shows requests, not usage: for citations, look at Bing.
Group the hits by the bot's purpose. Google-Extended does not show up in the log: it is only a robots.txt token; the one that crawls is Googlebot.
Anyone can write "GPTBot" in the User-Agent. Check the IP against the official lists the companies publish. And a 403 for an AI bot is usually a CDN block, not robots.txt.

secoes.legenda: Notify Bing, then check the log to see who really came.

texto: Check in Bing Webmaster that the sitemap was read successfully (course 1, lesson 3). Without this, neither AI Performance nor IndexNow pays off.
Publish the key in a .txt file at the site root and notify the new URLs after each publication. The method's script checks for the 200 before notifying.
At INEMA: 109 URLs notified with a 202 response on 09/24/2026 and 90 URLs with 200 on 10/02/2026.
On the server (nginx or Apache), copy the access log to your computer. Behind a CDN, use the CDN's log: the server's log only sees what got past it.
A person's IP is personal data (LGPD): before showing it to anyone, keep only the bot lines.
Run botlog (inemaseo-sistemas, MIT) or filter by hand on User-Agent. Look at three things: which purpose shows up, how many fakes there are, and whether any search bot got a 403.

exemplo.texto: Only training bots in the log and no search bots: the site may be outside the index of the search AIs. Check robots.txt and the CDN (course 1, lesson 6).

secoes.sub: The first block is from the inemaSEO method (model only: it needs your key). The second reads the log on your computer; detailed teaching in course 7.

blocos.conteudo:
# urls.txt: one URL per line, all on the same host
# the IndexNow key is published at https://seusite.com/<chave>.txt
INDEXNOW_KEY=<chave> tools/avisar_buscadores.sh urls.txt
# checks that each URL returns 200 before notifying; stops if any does not return 200

git clone https://github.com/inematds/inemaseo-sistemas && cd inemaseo-sistemas/ferramentas/botlog
# copy the server log (read-only)
ssh usuario@SEU_SERVIDOR 'cd /var/log/nginx; zcat -f access.log.*.gz; cat access.log.1 access.log' > /tmp/site.log
# report by purpose, with the IP checked against the official lists
python3 botlog.py analisar /tmp/site.log --sitemap https://seusite.com/sitemap.xml --saida saida/site
# LGPD: before sharing, keep only the bot lines with an official IP
python3 botlog.py filtrar /tmp/site.log --saida /tmp/so-robos.log

abas.html:
botlog on the real log of desenho.inema.pro (10/05 to 10/19/2026), already filtered to only bots with an official IP:

8 linhas, 8 de robô (treino 6, busca 2); falsos 0

robo           finalidade  acessos  paginas  robots_txt  4xx/5xx
GPTBot         treino      4        2        0           0
ClaudeBot      treino      2        2        1           0
OAI-SearchBot  busca       2        1        2           1

In the repository's assembled sample (documentation IPs, official User-Agents), the report flags:

  • 4 fakes: GPTBot, Googlebot and PerplexityBot coming from an IP outside the official list.
  • A 403 for ClaudeBot, which simulates a CDN block.
  • A sitemap page that no bot read.

• The log shows a request, not a citation.
  • Behind a CDN, the IP may be the CDN's: use its log.
  • An old IP list creates false "fakes": update it.

secoes.sub: No access to the log? Do E2 with the example from the repository.

exercicios.texto: Check the sitemap in Bing Webmaster, publish the IndexNow key, and notify 3 new or changed URLs that return 200.
exercicios.pronto: Bing shows the sitemap with a success status and the IndexNow notification returned 200 or 202.

exercicios.texto: Run botlog on your site's log (or on the REAL example in the repository) and note the requests by purpose, the fakes, and the 403s for AI bots.
exercicios.pronto: a note with the count by purpose (search, user action, training), the number of fakes, and the list of 403s (or "none").

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: "ChatGPT uses the Bing index." How do you say this honestly?
opcoes: It is a fact documented by OpenAI.
A Seer study found 87% of citations in the Bing top 20; it is a small study, not a statement from OpenAI.
perguntas.explica: A hint from a study, with a small sample. A good reason to notify Bing, not a promise about ChatGPT.

perguntas.p: The log shows 30 requests from "GPTBot" coming from an IP outside OpenAI's list. What are they?
opcoes: A fake bot: someone using the name in the User-Agent.
perguntas.explica: Anyone can write a User-Agent. Without the IP on the official list, do not count it as an OpenAI bot.

perguntas.p: OAI-SearchBot gets a 403 in the log, but robots.txt allows it. Where do you look?
opcoes: In the CDN or the firewall: that is what really blocks.
perguntas.explica: robots.txt asks; the CDN enforces. A 403 for an AI bot is usually a CDN rule.

perguntas.p: Why does searching for Google-Extended in the log not work?
opcoes: Because it uses a secret IP.
Because it is only a robots.txt token; the one that crawls is Googlebot.
Because it only shows up in Bing.
perguntas.explica: Google-Extended controls use for training Gemini, with no bot of its own. It does not affect Google Search.

itens.texto: Notify with IndexNow only URLs that return 200; Bing feeds Copilot and the only citations dashboard.
Read by purpose, check the IP, and look for 403s on AI bots.
ChatGPT–Bing is a hint from a Seer study, not a statement from OpenAI. A log shows requests, not citations.
